title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
hook: Split the difference between multi-head and multi-query attention: share KV heads across groups of query heads and get most of the memory savings with little quality loss.
key_points: Groups query heads and assigns one shared key/value head per group, reducing KV cache size proportionally.
Multi-head attention (one KV per query head) and multi-query attention (one KV for all) are special cases of GQA.
Speeds up autoregressive decoding by shrinking the memory footprint the GPU must read each step.
Adopted in models like LLaMA 2 70B and Mistral 7B for efficient large-scale inference.
content_html: Ainslie et al. introduced Grouped-Query Attention as a practical middle ground between the quality of multi-head attention and the inference speed of multi-query attention. The key idea is to partition the query heads into G groups and give each group a single shared set of key and value heads, cutting KV cache size by a factor of G compared to standard multi-head attention.
extra_html:
How it works

In standard multi-head attention, each of H query heads has its own key head and value head. Multi-query attention collapses this to one KV pair shared by all H query heads. GQA sits in between: divide H query heads into G groups, give each group one KV head. At inference time, each decoding step loads G times fewer KV vectors, which reduces memory bandwidth pressure - the dominant bottleneck during autoregressive generation.

Why it matters

Decoding speed is often memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound, so shrinking the KV cache directly translates to faster token generation. Ainslie et al. show GQA matches multi-head quality much more closely than multi-query attention does, making it a near-free lunch for large models. See the paper on arXiv for benchmarks and ablations.

related.title: Multi-Query Attention: Faster Decoding
related.hook: Share one key/value head across all query heads - the KV cache shrinks by a factor of H and decoding gets dramatically faster with barely any quality cost.

related.title: FlashAttention: Fast, Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
related.hook: Attention got faster not by approximating it, but by being smarter about GPU memory — never writing the giant attention matrix out to slow memory.

related.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA)
related.hook: Quadratic attention chokes at a million tokens. MiniMax runs exact attention over only a Top-k of key-value blocks per query group — cutting per-token attention compute ~28x at 1M context.

related.title: Grouped Query Experts: MoE Inside Attention
related.hook: Mixture-of-experts usually routes whole feed-forward layers. Grouped Query Experts routes attention query heads instead — matching a dense baseline while firing half of them per token.

flashcards.back_html: It partitions the query heads into G groups and gives each group one shared key/value head, cutting KV cache size by a factor of G.

flashcards.prompt: Why does shrinking the KV cache speed up autoregressive decoding?

choices.text: Decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound, so reading fewer KV vectors per step is faster
It reduces the number of floating-point multiplications per token
It lets the model skip attention layers entirely

flashcards.explanation_html: Decoding is dominated by memory bandwidth, not compute; loading fewer KV vectors each step reduces that bottleneck.

flashcards.prompt: How do multi-head and multi-query attention relate to GQA?

choices.text: They are the two extreme special cases of GQA (one KV per head, and one KV for all)
They are unrelated architectures GQA replaces
They both use more KV heads than query heads

flashcards.explanation_html: Multi-head (one KV per query head) and multi-query (one KV for all) are the endpoints; GQA sits in between with one KV per group.
